record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Let P and Q be directed complete posets whose Scott spaces Sigma P and Sigma Q are sober. Must the product dcpo P x Q, ordered coordinatewise, also be Scott sober, meaning that Sigma(P x Q) is sober?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6. Let P, Q be Scott sober dcpos. Must the product P × Q be Scott sober?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A directed complete partially ordered set (dcpo) is a poset $(P,\le)$ in which every directed subset has a supremum. The Scott topology on a dcpo $P$ has as its open sets those $U \subseteq P$ satisfying: (i) $U$ is an upper set (if $x \in U$ and $x \le y$ then $y \in U$), and (ii) for every directed subset $D \subseteq P$ with $\sup D \in U$, there exists $d \in D$ with $d \in U$. Write $\Sigma P$ for $P$ equipped with the Scott topology. A topological space $X$ is sober if every nonempty irreducible closed subset of $X$ is the closure of a unique point. Call a dcpo $P$ Scott sober if $\Sigma P$ is sober.

Given dcpos $P$ and $Q$ that are both Scott sober, equip the cartesian product $P \times Q$ with the coordinatewise order (so $(p_1,q_1) \le (p_2,q_2)$ iff $p_1 \le p_2$ and $q_1 \le q_2$), under which $P \times Q$ is itself a dcpo. Must $P \times Q$ be Scott sober, i.e., must $\Sigma(P \times Q)$ be sober?
artifact.category_tag: Sobriety of Scott topology on dcpos
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved in the negative: there exist two dcpos whose Scott spaces are both sober but whose order-product has non-sober Scott space. This is established in the arXiv preprint "Products of two sober dcpo's need not be sober" (arXiv:2408.08587, 2024), which explicitly states that it answers the open problem on sobriety of Scott spaces of products.

status_evidence.title: Products of two sober dcpo's need not be sober
status_evidence.snippet: two dcpo's whose Scott spaces are sober were constructed, but the Scott space of their order product is not sober, which answers an open problem on the sobriety of Scott spaces
status_evidence.claim: Provides a counterexample showing that the product of two Scott sober dcpos need not be Scott sober, thereby answering the question negatively.
